biography: Joel Schumann hails from the vibrant city of São Paulo, Brazil, where the roar of engines is as much a part of the soundscape as samba rhythms. Growing up near Interlagos, Joel’s passion for racing ignited early. He would spend hours watching Formula 1 cars scream past, dreaming of one day being behind the wheel himself. His break came unexpectedly. While working as a mechanic's apprentice, he filled in for a sick driver at a local karting event and stunned everyone by winning. This unexpected victory propelled him into the world of motorsport. He quickly rose through the ranks, showcasing a remarkable ability to adapt to different racing conditions. A defining moment came in the Brazilian GT Championship in 2018. Battling mechanical issues throughout the race, Joel nursed his ailing Puma GTB to a podium finish, demonstrating his exceptional car control and determination. Now at the peak of his career, Joel continues to compete at the highest level, a steady and respected figure in the racing community, known for his consistent performance and unwavering focus.
drivingStyle: Joel is known for his incredibly smooth and precise driving style. He is not one for flamboyant overtakes or risky maneuvers. Instead, he focuses on maintaining consistent pace, minimizing mistakes, and preserving his tires. He meticulously analyzes track conditions and adapts his driving accordingly. In corners, he favors a late apex, maximizing his exit speed. He is also remarkably calm under pressure, rarely cracking, even in the most intense race situations. His ability to manage tires, especially in endurance races, is considered one of his greatest strengths.

famousQuote: "Racing isn't about taking risks; it's about minimizing them while maximizing your opportunities."
careerHighlight: Winning the Brazilian GT Championship in 2020 after a season-long battle with Ricardo Vargas. He secured the title with a dominant performance in the final race at Interlagos, in front of his home crowd.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the 24 Hours of Interlagos in 2019 due to a mechanical failure while leading in the final hours. The disappointment was compounded by the fact that his team had worked tirelessly to prepare the car.
